extracted.intended_audience: law students, legal researchers, librarians, and attorneys conducting multi-jurisdictional state regulatory research
extracted.subtask_description: Finding and verifying state regulations, proposed regulations, administrative decisions, executive orders, and attorney general opinions across multiple jurisdictions using primary sources, subscription databases, and secondary treatises or surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult administrative law treatises
rubrics_metrics.description: To understand state regulatory powers and procedures, review Administrative Law and Practice and other treatises on administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatises cover state agencies and regulations on administrative procedures, rule-making, adjudication, oversight, litigation over specific types of issues, judicial review and more. See the Law Library's Administrative Law Treatises page for additional resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 50-state reviews and scholarship to learn state procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the regulatory and decision-making processes for your jurisdiction(s) by consulting multi-state studies and scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A 50-State Review of Regulatory Procedures (Mercatus Center, Apr 2022) examines each state's form of rulemaking, executive/legislative & agency review processes, impact analysis and periodic review requirements; Jason A. Schwartz's '52 Experiments with Regulatory Review' studied adherence to best practices. These resources help compare state rulemaking processes and oversight practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Westlaw, Lexis, and Bloomberg for state regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: State regulations, proposed regulations, and regulation-tracking are often available via Westlaw, Lexis, and Bloomberg Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Law Library provides links to these database resources. Be aware that coverage and features (e.g., tracking, historical coverage) vary by provider and by state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check state government websites for the most recent administrative codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The most recent versions of administrative codes may be found on a state's government website, usually on the Secretary of State's webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official state websites often carry current administrative codes; use them to verify currency and official status where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use law library state resource guides for direct links and print-code titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law Library's state resources guides provide direct links to regulation content on databases and state websites and list titles of print administrative codes (if still published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the relevant state resources guide for direct access points and bibliographic information about print administrative codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate administrative decisions in databases and agency websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Some state agencies' decisions are available on Westlaw, Lexis, and Bloomberg Law; administrative decisions may also be available directly on the state regulatory agency's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search both subscription databases and the relevant agency site to locate decisions, because availability differs by agency and state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Lexis coverage and use Regulation Tracking when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: In Lexis, state registers and regulation tracking are found in Administrative Codes & Regulations, but coverage varies by state; for some states Lexis no longer updates the register and provides rulemaking activity only through its Regulation Tracking service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation Tracking coverage is generally from 1990 to current. If the register isn't updated for a state, use the Regulation Tracking product to find proposals, notices, hearings, emergency and permanent promulgations, and withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and choose the appropriate Westlaw regulation databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Westlaw has separate/regime-specific regulation resources: historical regulations, proposed & adopted regulations - current, proposed & adopted regulations - all, and regulation tracking, with coverage varying by state and database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'historical regulations' for older materials (coverage varies), 'proposed & adopted regulations - current' for the two most recent years and newly proposed/adopted rules, and 'proposed and adopted regulations - all' to search the state's entire register (coverage starting from 2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Bloomberg Law's Rulemaking collection for various rule types
rubrics_metrics.description: In Bloomberg Law, proposed, final, emergency, temporary, and interim rules and regulatory notices are found under Rulemaking within the State Laws & Regulation collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search Bloomberg's State Laws & Regulation > Rulemaking to retrieve assorted rule types and notices for a state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check AALL Online Legal Information Resources for official status
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Association of Law Libraries' Online Legal Information Resources notes the official status of each state's primary law publications found on government websites, including regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AALL's resource to determine whether a state website's publication is the state's official version or an unofficial copy; this affects citation and verification practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate executive orders on governor and archive sites (and Westlaw)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most current governor's executive orders are typically on the state's governor webpage; historical orders may be on the state archive's website; Westlaw's State Executive Orders database may also contain orders (coverage from 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check governor pages first for current orders, state archives for historical orders, the Law Library guides for direct links, and Westlaw for orders (noting its 2008 coverage marker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Find attorney general opinions on AG websites and digitized repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent state attorney general opinions are typically found on the state's attorney general webpage; current and historical opinions may be digitized on HeinOnline State Attorney General Reports and Opinions and LLMC Digital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using LLMC Digital, filter first by State, then by Category: 'Attorney General Publications' to locate opinions. Use AG webpages for the most recent opinions and HeinOnline/LLMC for historic runs.
